executive_summary:
Recommendation: move the wordpress MySQL database to three purpose-built AWS services in three waves. Wave 1 moves it 1:1 to Aurora MySQL, which serves 62.6% of the queries. Wave 2 puts ElastiCache in front of 15 hot reads, which carry 77.5% of calls. Wave 3 moves the other 37.4% of the queries to DynamoDB. The target schemas are designed. The projected cost is $505 per month at AWS Price List on-demand prices for us-east-1, retrieved 2026-10-19. No current cost was collected for the source database, so the plan claims no saving against it.

Risk: overall risk is medium. Two exposures drive it: keeping the DynamoDB tables in sync with Aurora MySQL through change data capture, and the queries where two engines scored almost the same. Test the replication and confirm where those queries run before wave 3 starts.

Decision: approve wave 1. It keeps the same engine family as MySQL and its current data model, and the cutover waits until schema and data parity is validated against the source.
